We will consider the matrix $$ A = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp 1 \\ -2 \amp -3 \amp -2 \\ 3 \amp 7 \amp 4 \\ \end{array}\right] $$ and begin performing Gaussian elimination without using partial pivoting.

Perform two row replacement operations to find the row equivalent matrix $$ A' = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.} $$ Find elementary matrices $E_1$ and $E_2$ that perform these two operations so that $E_2E_1 A = A'$.

Perform a third row replacement to find the upper triangular matrix $$ U = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.} $$ Find the elementary matrix $E_3$ such that $E_3E_2E_1A = U$.

We can write $A=E_1^{-1}E_2^{-1}E_3^{-1} U$. Find the inverse matrices $E_1^{-1}$, $E_2^{-1}$, and $E_3^{-1}$ and the product $L = E_1^{-1}E_2^{-1}E_3^{-1}$. Then verify that $A=LU$.

Suppose that we want to solve the equation $A\xvec = \bvec = \threevec4{-7}{12}$. We will write $$ A\xvec = LU\xvec = L(U\xvec) = \bvec $$ and introduce an unknown vector $\cvec$ such that $U\xvec = \cvec$. Find $\cvec$ by noting that $L\cvec = \bvec$ and solving this equation.

Now that we have found $\cvec$, find $\xvec$ by solving $U\xvec = \cvec$.

Using the factorization $A=LU$ and this two-step process, solve the equation $A\xvec = \threevec{2}{-2}{7}$.
